text: Met my friend here for a purchase of something I bought from her and Fox's was the designated spot, because it's iconic in the area.  It has plenty of parking, has plenty of light and allowed us to see each other easily.

This LARGE dry cleaners (and tailoring) is located at the corner of 17 & Arch.  Great location for the  and nearby .  They have cleaned a few items for me at a good price and well done.  They also cleaned and preserved my wedding gown.  (Ouch - that price!!!!!)  I also had a zipper replaced on an expensive jacket.  It cpst $35 to have the new zipper put in, which seemed really high to me, but iot was better than replacing the jacket. (Which would have been a few hundred bucks.)  Ladies who run the place are nice and the computerized systems helps ensure your stuff is really YOUR stuff.

I love some kebabs and I was excited the website said they were planning lamb roasts every .  The chicken and falafel sandwiches are alright but the lamb pastrami is the best thing I've had here.  I could tell that they really take some time to use some quality ingredients in a lot of what they prepare but they still have a lot of kinks to work out.  One of their unique offerings is the young coconut they pop open for you to drink.    Areas that could use some improvement:  They didn't have any self-serve ice next to the drinks so that was a bit of a challenge.  They also got my tables order confused with a to go order so that caused a bit of mix up so they need to develop a better order system.  Something got burned and caused a really bad burned odor and fumes; so accidents happen but maybe a better venting system over the oven could help it from being so overwhelming a sensation when they do.    The website is a bit confusing with the hours listing being  and 3PM-12PM in different locations on the site so that needs to be cleaned up to fix  confusion.  The environment was also a bit confused inside with half art gallery and half restaurant and I  don't think the art gallery did much for me other than limit my seating options.  The crowd consisted of a lot of really dirty unwashed gutter punks and other  hipster types that gave off quite a bit of unpleasant body odor so just be prepared for the possibility that if enough of them are there you might want to just get a to-go order to avoid their retched stench.  I think the  restaurants might want to start posting signs that say, "No shower no service!"    50 cent surcharge for using credit cards!  I completely understand how credit cards abuse business owners with their fees but you should at least post a sign stating that policy instead of telling folks after the fact or NOT telling them at all!  The specials board is very badly placed way over to the left where nobody will see it unless they know to look way over to the left above the drinks.  You need the specials right underneath the register where folks can see them as they are approaching to order so they know they are there and really you should hang a board above the register.  Overall there are just a whole lot of other  and  restaurants that have better food to me at this point in the city but I certainly see this joint has some potential if they get their act together as they are the only restaurant of this genre in the .  So I'm just going to wait and see what develops but I'm still going to go back to try the roast lamb and get another coconut.

At last - I am a  virgin no longer.  And what a way to go.  It was  in  for  and DH & I went to  but the line was so long that we decided to go acrosss the street to the sports bar.  Afetr a round of fried goodnees - DH had the cheese fries and I had some really outstanding O-rings - we were on to our main attraction.  DH had a cheese steak with Provolone and it was terrific. I enjoyed a garlicky plate of Veal Scallopini that was kickin' in old school.  This was THE $#!T - for real.  Mushrooms, green peppers, onions and tender veal (wish there had been a bit more of that) in a garlicky, olive-oily sauce that reminded me of how my  woulda done it.  Um.  If I'd had an  Nonna.  Can't wait to go back and try the Chicken Sandwich with Spinach.  I am sold on .

The third child of New Leaf Cuisine (Manayunk & Broomall being the elder siblings), Purple has replaced the ill fated  at  location in . While "Asian Fusion" is often just confusion, this house seems to actually know what it's doing when it comes to Sushi and  food.   Their menu is a complex of decent sushi, "Street Food," noodles and  dishes, all well done with a touch of creativity and lots of flavor. Prices reflect the talent in the kitchen, so even the dim sum small plates add up fast. As a first timer, and suspecting that Mandarin was the primary language, we opted for that part of the menu to sample.   Smart move.  Our four dishes were; Beef Chow Fun (traditional  broad noodles), Chicken with Dry Pepper (medium heat w jicama for cool crunch) from  Kitchen - Entrees, Spicy Crispy Chicken (crunchy fried chicken  style) and Wok-fried  (hottest dish w  spice sensibilities). They were all very good, with tender sliced beef, white meat chicken and no skimping on the spices nor portions. Three of us supped to our hearts' content with leftovers for . Each made its own statement without redundancy. The kitchen was well trained in the mystic art of  sauces.   If the sushi and other  pieces are on par with the mainland portion of the menu, Purple Leaf could well be worthy of that fifth star. As it is, it is a giant leap forward for the local  restaurant scene.
My kid and all her friends LOVE it here. Especially  with steak or shrimp (extra charge).

It is so simple. Check-in, name called, blood drawn and you're on your way.   I had no idea this location was so close to home. I have always used the Quest closer to my doctors office, stopping by on my way home. This time I had to have blood drawn  before seeing a specialist, so I Googled Quest and found this location which is conveniently located in my hood. It is hidden on the backside of the building so it is unnoticeable as you drive by the medical building. Out of site, out of mind.   I did not go on-line and make an appointment ahead of time. I just showed up, signed my name on the registry and took a seat. I barely had time to check in on Yelp and my name was being called. I presented the technician with my paperwork, insurance card and ID. She quickly got busy, preparing the vacutainer tubes as I tried to relax listening to the music playing from a small boom box she had sitting on the floor. I HATE having my blood drawn and have veins that most technicians hate. My veins are small, roll and hide when it is time to be poked and drained. My tech was not chatty, but she was professional. I give her four stars because, she jabbed me without hurting me and got in a vein on the first poke. I was In and Out in nothing flat, it was express service at its' best.   Now that I know a Quest is near my home, I may make this location my choice for blood draws. Instead of using the one near my doctors office, I'll come here. When I'm  finished here, I can get myself a treat at Starbucks or  which both are conveniently located across the street. You get a treat when you donate blood, why not get one after having a blood draw.
We buy liquor here on occaision because it is convenient. I think the PA liquor laws are really strange and generally nonsensical.

My second visit to  in  after  absence.  is coming back to life, and the area close to  seems to be spearheading the revival. It is great to see a renaissance in this old river city.  It has suffered hard times through some neglectful governments and perhaps not so fatherly town elders. Yet, it is hard to keep a good old ville down when it has natural beauty and a real purpose over .  So it is with the King George II Inn. Originally built to be close to the ferry to , , the only way across this water course for  AFTER the ferry was started, the KGII evolved into a restaurant and subsequently an inn. Sitting in the oldest part of the building, the tavern, it is easy to imagine what it was like to be living and traveling in colonial .  The various farmers, businessmen, hucksters, cons, grifters, and cutthroats gathered here to do their business, and wait for the ferry to take them to the colony of .   Even , that historic atmosphere permeates the . Certainly there are ghosts stories aplenty.  I stopped into the  for late lunch, sitting at a small table at the window overlooking the bottom of , and the river just beyond.  The server (who was as gracious as an owner) greeted me warmly, took my order, and left me to my mental wandering.  The Pierogies appeared on a long thin white dish, covered in sautéed onions and fresh chives. A dollop of sour cream occupied one corner.  They were lightly fried, potato and cheese. They were pretty good at 6 for $9. I knew I was paying for the privilege of location.  No complaints.  The Tavern itself was excellently preserved and rehabbed to feel very original. All dark woods, heavy oak tables, and mirrored bar.  A perfect place to reenact debates between Patriots and  over lagers and locally distilled whiskey.    It is certainly worth a visit and a meal if you are into  history.  It is not quite , , where the entire community is a historic park and everyone is in costume.  Still, with a little imagination it is capable of taking you on quite a trip.

This is a brand new gas station (Exxon at the moment) and convenience store.  The space is super clean (as it should be since it's brand new). The gas station portion is well lit.  Do not confuse this with the Original Brown Derby which is across  from this location and sells hot plates. I do wonder if they are affiliated or all appropriating a traditional name.

restaurant before the beach at . If you come at  Brunch, please make reservations, they are fully booked most of the time. I have been here twice. I think I can give them a fair review. Their restaurant is at exclusive area and need toll if you from I-275.   My friend and me visited them during job assignment near the beach. We got daily special . This is a special dish in  cook with ground beef and potato.  is  know as potatoes man. He promoted the potatoes in the local. This dish also very similar to shepherd pie in .   The second dish . The last time the locksmith came to my house? I hugged him. That's how much I love their service.   My house is old; they are doing beaucoup construction work in my neighborhood causing my house to shift on it's foundations. Locks don't like shifting foundations, so sometimes they spaz out. Or you discover that there's a button lock on the front door that gets accidentally pushed and how do you get OUT?! So I just call up the office and someone comes out usually with  (weekdays).   I have had a variety of locksmiths come out but my favorite is the older man because he reminds me of my grandfather. (He's also the one I hugged last time. Yes I think he thought I was crazy.) Everyone has been very professional and really helpful, giving me hints on how to prevent future problems.  I know they have gift items in their store and really should get over there and shop.

When this new IHOP opened, it wasn't open  any day of the week. I am now happy to say, it has expanded it's  for  to .  This location use to be a 's Diner that closed  and sat vacant. IHOP came in did a full remodel and has brought new life and a new breakfast place to the  area.   Part of my work schedule requires me to work in  on weekends and except for the local McDonald's the choices for an early breakfast were bleak. Now that this IHOP has expanded its , my options have expanded. I can easily stop in grab a quick coffee and a Simple Breakfast and still be at work by .   Their Simple Breakfast is a good value. It's simple, two eggs, choice of two bacon strips or two sausage patties,  and Toast. I have them hold the toast, the Hash Browns are enough starch for this dieting man.   The staff from what I have experienced is small town friendly and attentive to their diners. I may find myself getting up a little earlier just so I can have a hearty breakfast. After all, it is the most important meal of .

Found this little place when i checked YELP to see what was in the local area. I'm glad I popped on by. It was a beautiful  and the outside tables were busy so the husbeast and I opted to sit at one of the large communal tables inside after we placed our breakfast orders.   Inside, it's decorated in a fun, ecclectic way, that speaks to different cultures.  Dia de los Muertos skulls are around as is other iconic statuary. There's a warm and homey feeling that just exudes friendlyness and the locals seem to like the place.    The food too, speaks of the love the people have for what's offered. I had an omelet with ham and cheese and some of their home fries, the husband had one of their burritos, all the food was delicious and well made. everything tasted fresh! And let me tell you about their coffee! It was AMAZING!

Excellent burgers on , just where Passyunk intersects with the 5. Design your own using the three computer stations, or go to the counter to talk with the people working there. Either way you get a standard double  complemented any way you choose. If you don't want to think that much about it, the menu offers several great combinations that are bound to make you happy.   Just the right amount of grease, potato or pretzel roll, natural sugar carbonated beverages,  ice cream based shakes, and fresh fruit smoothies, all surround the ultimate comfort food for your indulgence.   Prices that won't break the bank just off the hippest street in town.   If there is something to improve upon, it is that it appears that every burger is finished to well done regardless of how you request it. Still, they are so juicy I almost didn't notice.

It is huge improvement when there is staff members help you to get the right order. A beeper was given when your food is ready to pick. At least they no longer let the customers to figure out the food on the counter.   We were here for  to celebrate the administrative day. Most of my guest got two tacos and a drink with about $10. I got the grilled fish and grilled shrimp. It is tasty for the two tacos I have selected. I like the grilled shrimp better. It has some blackened seasoning on it.   I got the margarita for my combination deal. The margarita start light then feel the alcohol effects later. We enjoy our time there.

Now that I am working in this area, I must confess that I am frequenting  far too often - however the Craft 2 menu allows me to eat one, save one - and thus not consume the requisite 750 cal minimum.  (Beans plus rice plus any meat choice = about 660 alone).  Also the "new" whole wheat tortilla is 270 cals (not 330). Additionally, they introduced a slightly spicy brown rice (a few calories less per serving than the white) in .  I don;t like it though, so I still get the bad-for-you-white rice.  Still, a cheap, calorie-bomb on the go. Oh - and I have to give a shout-out to  - the cute (nearly looks like L'il !) cashier who is super cool and friendly.

I go to Le Bon Temps often and they have some good music.  They also have FREE oysters on  but they go quick so you need to get there early!  The kitchen serves food til pretty late and I don't even know when they close it down so that is an option to keep in mind.  The bar is divided into 2 main areas with the front being full of pool tables and the back where the bands play.  This is usually a really fun bar to watch music until the point that it gets too crowded, which is way too often, but you always have the front area of the bar to escape to.    The back area, where the bands play, can just get miserably crowded especially on  when Soul Rebels play (it also is a bad "tradition" that the Soul Rebels NEVER start on time so it is like  or  they start usually so if you have to work  that really is a challenge).  There are also some people that take their pool games WAY too seriously in here and I've seen a few fights break out over a stupid game so don't get in those folks way.  Parking can sometimes be a bit of a challenge but if you get far enough away you can always find a spot.      They usually have pretty quick bar service and I usually prefer the front bar when there is music as it is quicker to get served than fighting the often formidable crowd in the back.  There is always an interesting crowd here and there is a special plaque on the bar involving a historical person that I will let you discover yourself.  There always seems to be something going on here when it seems nothing else is anywhere else in the area.  FYI:  This is yet another of the bars that claims the notoriety of having had  as a frequent customer.

I really liked the wild berry smoothie and the  V sandwich I had here.  Both were ready in a matter of  and were full of flavor.  The smoothie was super cold and almost gave me brain freeze upon three different occasions!  It was so good which was so tempting.    The sandwich was grilled with portobello, provolone, roasted red peppers, fresh spinach, and garlic aioli.  Very tasty and with a bit of a chew getting through the different textures in the sandwich.  Very colorful sandwich, as well.  I definitely recommend this!  Since I am in the neighborhood about once a month, I would probably stop in again, but even at lunch time, there was little to no conversation.  Nobody smiling.  Maybe that's just the way restaurants / coffee shops are now.  Everyone is on their phone or laptop and many have earphones in.  Sad that conversation seems to be non-existent in these types of places.  I remember "in " when these types of places were great for discussion on world problems, without getting into name calling.  Different times.  Oh, back to the review:  This is one of those places where the menu is on a chalkboard and you pay up front and wait for your order to be set on a counter when the staff calls out the order.  No names are taken, so if you want your order as soon as it is placed on the counter, you have to pay attention.  The staff just call out what is on the counter and I don't know what happens if two people have the same sandwich.  Not a great business model, but I guess they make it work.  I had to ask what the staff said because I wasn't paying attention when they shouted.  (I only caught part of the description.)  Maybe if they said something like "order up!" before announcing the items it would give more time to redirect my thinking.  Oh well, nobody else seemed to mind.  I'm glad there are still options that go that extra step.  Not so much here.  So only a four.  Review #313

Guapos Tacos are served street-style, with the protein taking center stage and chopped onions and cilantro plus light sauces adding to the flavor.   My first experience was at  industry night . There I tried tacos de lengua (tongue), tacos de carnitas and veggie tacos. The standouts were the lengua and veggie. The tongue was tender like a filet and the accompanying sauce had a tangy flavor. The veggie taco had flavorful, marinated grilled veggies.   My second taste of  was at . The grilled mahi mahi taco with a generous splash of hot sauce (from the selection of sauces on the ledge built into the the truck) was so delicious, I gladly waited in line again for .   The truck is colorful and fun and the guys who work inside are personable and handle crowds well. Two thumbs up for this tasty taco truck!

Hmmm this bar used to be a place. The bartender said "Round Up", but that didn't sound familiar to me. What was this place??  ANYWAY. We came here because I was in search of music and this bar...didn't have music. Womp. Oh well. They DID have All Day IPA, so I was pretty happy. You can sit at the bar or you can sit outside on the PATIO! Yeah, that's right, this place has a patio complete with a light up tree, tons of seating and a blow up pool. Did I get in the pool? NAH. But I did dig the patio and the vibe out there was fantastic. I just wish that it was a smidge cooler so that I can really hang out and soak up the atmosphere. This is definitely going to be a destination once fall arrives.

It is a really large and old oak tree that hosts weddings, picnics and just goofing around (not to be confused with the Dueling Oak in ).  It was here long before any of us were and will probably outlast all of us and maybe the next few generations after.  As a good strong and wise oak it would make all the ancient and modern Druids proud.  Respect the oak and do not break or otherwise harm the oak or despoil it with graffiti or the curse of the Druids will be upon thee and if I catch you doing it you will be wearing a wig of  moss for awhile as this tree is under my protection and I will call you out for a visit to the Dueling Oak in .

Sweet, Mother of God!  is amazing.   I can not tell you the last time I had something this good in my mouth. I could, but one of us (me) might blush. From the first bite of Terrine, to the last bite of Creme Brûlée my taste buds were screaming, "OMG, don't stop, faster, give it to me faster, I want more."   Proving that every dish was a foodgasm.   We started off with a Terrine, which was made with chicken liver and bone marrow. I am not a fan of liver, especially chicken and this Terrine won me over. It was served in a small mason jar with crostini's on the side. I had no idea, a chicken liver could taste so good.   I love escargot and this is the best I've had in my entire life. I bet even  would have skipped using ketchup and enjoyed these exquisite snails. They were served with bone marrow and with the two of them combined on a baguette, totally set off fireworks in my mouth. If you are a fan of both of these culinary delights, you'll understand how delicious it would be when they're combined into one.   Next we enjoyed two pots of mussels. A la Marimiere, was a traditional white wine shallot broth and , a tomato, garlic and fresh basil broth. They were served in small black pots on plates with slices of baguette on the side. When the top was removed, it was the perfect place to discard the shells. It made it so easy to shuck all the mussels at once. I was then able to enjoy my mussels with a soup spoon as if I were eating a hearty soup. When I was done, I wanted to pick up the pot by its' handles and do my best  imitation, "More, please".   We were both stuffed like the  turkey, but it did not stop us from exploring the dessert menu. If you're going to over stuff yourself, why only share one dessert? You might as well, go hog wild and experience two. We ordered the Belgium Waffles with Baked Apples and Cheesecake with Cherries and Candied Bacon. The bartender claimed the Cheesecake was his favorite, so I ordered it instead of my original intention Creme Brûlée.  The house made cheesecake with the candied cherries and bacon was unbelievable. Forget about breaking me off a piece of that Kit Kat Bar, break me off another piece of that candied bacon, it is so addicting. The Belgium Waffles with baked apples was like eating an ready to assembled pie. It was a great way to end our meal.   As a bonus, the bartender treated us to a Creme Brûlée. He wanted to make sure, he didn't steer me wrong on ordering his favorite. He was right his was the best of the three, but the Creme Brûlée was still outstanding. I'd be torn on which one to reorder on my next visit.   The ambiance is a mixture of blast from the past  (classic cocktail lounge) and as  stated, "industrial chic". It is both relaxing and romantic.  This is an ideal place for , business meeting or hanging with friends. The staff is extremely friendly and very knowledgeable about the menu offerings. I was so impressed, I plan on being a regular at Tripel.

Accessories is really the name of the game here. I was hopping down  when I came across this cute boutique. They have really cute clothes, but the jewelry and sunglasses were out of this world! With the help of the awesome employees, I was able to find the perfect gift for a friend- a pair of mirrored sunglasses that are both stylish and useful. The clothes here are light and perfect for the impending warmer weather and they come in lots of bright colors. Prices are a little steep, but the sunglasses I found were reasonable and seemed worth the money.
We saw "Menopause: The Musical" here  - but the sound was so loud it was deafening!!!  Otherwise - a great small theatre with decent productions at moderate prices.

Don't get it. Seriously, I do not understand all these 5 Star reviews for these donuts. I was not impressed. I stopped by when my favorite radio station was broadcasting live, expecting to be blown away. It didn't happen.   I always judge a donut shop by their  Chocolate Long Johns and the one I had here was dry and rather flavorless. It was chewy and a bottle of milk didn't even help. I think my second one was a Buttermilk type donut. This one, I took only a single bite and threw it back in the bag. Yeah, it was that good.   It had to be an off day, they were slammed with a popular radio station in their parking lot. Next time I'm headed south to shop at Costco, I'll detour and give them a second chance. As of now, I think the donuts at TDS are just average. A Long John at QT is fresher and better.   The staff was friendly and I liked that the young lady asked if I wanted my  plain or creme filled. Customer Service was good and they kept up with the busy crowd.   I'll be back? - Everyone deserves a second chance.   When:  Why: 1st Experience - Radio Broadcast
Closing for good/Going out of Business . Everything at least 50% off - selling down to the bare walls.

Great new spot in the LGD! Look for the new build building and they are in the back on the left as you face the courtyard. I say this because the door is inset a little. Thanks goodness for their triangle floor sign... that's not their name but you know what I'm talking about.  I've been 2x already and had an assortment of cocktails. On one of , I had a lovely glass of bubbles and sampled a Boulevardier. The other night with the fabulous Shercole, I tried , at first I though the Pernod might be too much for me, but that was just the first sip. Refreshing and delicious. Second I had , so tasty and citrusy.   I also tried the pimento cheese on a saltine which is stupidly delicious and the carrot puree which pops with ginger.  Service was great. And the atmosphere is well designed and fun. The outdoor courtyard is great... when it's not 80bajillion degrees.

I like steak N Shake because I can usually trust their burgers to be fresh.   What I I found utterly ridiculous about this particular location was that I waited  in the drive through after placing my order. When I got to the window, and I was ready to pay, The girl there, handed me my bag and said "Thanks, have ."   Nope, she didn't take payment. "I haven't paid yet." So the girl behind her told her to collect the money. She did, gave me the correct change and all that. then wished me . "Can I have my drink?" She looked behind her. "Is this your drink?" Honestly, how am I supposed to know? I'm not inside the location.  "is it a large diet? Then it's mine." I'm polite, but seriously, make sure that your folks are trained before you put them on the window.

This is definitely a better tour with a car than doing it via Riverboat but the boat is a nice cruise.  This is the site of the historic victory over the  at  which is celebrated in  with the statue of Gen. .  That notorious pirate  and his band helped out but the real star of the battle was the artillery that decimated the  troops.  Mostly this is just a big field with some signs along with a few historical sites and the graveyard.  My dad is a big history  and he brought me out here often when I was a kid.  I haven't had a chance to check out the new visitor's center.

Finally tried the pricey  restaurant and had 5 star service (and 4 star fare) on the lovely outdoor deck.  Salmon was tender ($26 for lunch!!!!) and Burger ($18!!!) on a Brioche bun with sauteed mushrooms and onions was very good also.  Super pricey (even with 10% off for members) but a fun and special experience. Great for Mother's Day (come a different day and celebrate your mom) or a proposal dinner.

Five stars for Hawthorne Painting! I was driving near my neighborhood when I spotted a sign for this company, and I pulled it up on  as soon as I got home. I sent a request a quote message and ended up chatting with , the owner, . He stopped by to see my project, sent me a quote, and within  he and his crew were at my house!   We needed our front railing, front door, and roof deck railings to be sanded down and re-painted. Our house is  but, as we've discovered, new construction doesn't always equal the best quality.  and his crew showed up bright and early around 8:30am, and worked tirelessly in the sun until the project was finished .    explained the differences in the types of paint he needed to use for the railings and door. Everyone in the crew was friendly and careful about their work space - by the time they left, you wouldn't have known they were even here, aside from their gorgeous handiwork! My husband and I think the railings and door look even better now than they did when we bought our house.   My only regret? Not taking before and after photos! These guys made a world of difference and I'm so happy every time I look at my front door. I highly recommend  and wouldn't hesitate to hire them again for another project.

I stepped inside the  for  and, right, it hasn't changed. Tiny hole in the wall bar that serves cheap drinks. Really who isn't a fan of that? Do not expect fanciness. Order a straight pour or regular mixed drink or a beer.  Cash only but there is an ATM inside  Since it's carnival season, the door was standing wide open and they had made containers of hurricanes and trays of jello shots (and, yes, I bought jello shots for my Mom but she said they were too vodka-y. My Mom, the gourmand of jello shots)  The bar is as smoky as ever (which is why I'm not a regular) so it will be interesting to see how it fairs after the smoking ban.   Also because it's carnival, there is a food truck parked outside everyday of parades.  it's .

This is really a small little spot that you might easily walk past and miss if you aren't paying attention but they certainly deserve your attention.  They have some good versions of items that not many other places in the area offer and then they offer some much better versions of items than many other  places seem to push out of their kitchens  which often seem like recently defrosted factory made food.  This place is similar to the quality and care in their food that  and  put out except they are more expensive while also offering items those other establishments don't.    The dumpling selection here definitely has more of a house made and not factory made (then frozen and reheated) texture to it like many of the other  restaurants offer so  really seems to be putting out among the best available dumplings in the area now. Their  chicken was well spiced and was a large serving of mostly meat for the price but I would appreciate more vegetables in the dish.  Their hot tea selection includes items I haven't seen in a long time and it was quite nice to have some golden buckwheat tea again after many years without seeing it as an option around these parts.  The hot and sour soup was well flavored but I noticed there was no wood ear fungus in it which I consider to be pretty essential to a proper and HEALTHY part of any hot and sour soup.    The service was very attentive and kept the drinks refilled along with dealing well with my grumpy dining companion that was just all surly over several of the menu options being sold out already (do come earlier than later as they seem to often sell out of items ).  The only big area of improvement I would argue for is that they could offer more dishes without pork as quite a large portion of the menu contains pork mixed in without even saying it is in there in true  style but in the  some more pork free options would be nice and accurately labeling the dishes with pork in them on the menu would be appreciated.    Overall I certainly look forward to more visits here to sample more of the menu.

This is a review of my Covid-19 testing experience; I never set foot inside the hospital as all testing is taking place outside, in the driveway off of , .   I recently returned from a trip to . Despite taking proper precautions during my travels, I wanted to get tested for my own peace of mind and to ensure that I would not unknowingly expose anyone if I was an asymptomatic virus carrier. (You can select three types of toppings which is included in the price.)  I stepped over to watch the process unfold, then refold.  Basically, the ingredients are continuously mixed and spread thin to freeze them over and over.  Then additional flavors are added based upon your selection.  Once all those have been added, the ice cream is shaped like a large square which is then slowly scraped into a roll shape.  There were five rolls about 3 inches across and they were stacked on their ends inside a paper cup.  Then, your toppings are carefully added (the ends of the rolls are taller than the cup, so they don't want the toppings falling off.)    There are self serve napkins and sturdy spoons which are needed.  The ice cream is very cold and until it warms a bit, can require a bit of pressure from the spoon to get through the rolled ice cream.  Fortunately, the spoon was equal to the challenge and I was able to enjoy my treat.  Be aware that these are full cup servings.  I didn't see any options on the menu board for different sizes.  So, either come with an appetite, or bring a friend who likes the same choices you do!  Good flavor, fun to watch, and lots of options to make the ice cream fit your taste.  Review #1186

Approaching  (Rosemary) Restaurant on a rainy  takes a bit of courage.  The store front is a rowhouse with a neon "Open" sign in the window and an old unlit sign beneath it. Walked back across the street and up the front steps of 925.  On the first door to the left was the restaurant sign bidding we enter.  What was behind the door?   I went in first.  I was greeted by an apartment converted into a small eatery.  Yellow walls, stained wood trim. Wall sconces, but little other adornment.  No one else in the main dining area.  We stood a moment and waited to see if someone would come out to seat us.   later a woman appeared from the rear with a warm smile and firm voice welcoming us to her shop.  She was the owner, hostess, and chef.  Very big persona.  Lovely, and I immediately relaxed.  At  we expected other patrons, but we were the first and only folks there .  She sat us at a central table for 4, allowing us to spread out.  NFL Playoffs had depleted her clientele, but we were quite happy to have all her attention.    After getting the lay of the land from the gracious Madame, we ordered off the rather small menu, which is in both English and .  The Polish Plate to share as our appetizer.  It consisted of Meat Pierogies, Potato Pancakes, Kielbasa in , and Apple Sauce.  The Pierogies were the least enjoyable part of the dish. While the dough was lightly fried and was a good consistency, the meat was too dense and organ-tasting for me. The Potato Pancakes were large and thin, not very oily, and a good mix of potato and flour (to hold them together).  They were crispy on the edges and tasty with a dollop of Apple Sauce to mix a little sweetness with the mild saltiness of the latke. The Kielbasa was excellent.  Scored before grilling to help the heat penetrate and to avoid splitting, the outer skin was just firm enough to hold the link together, but when bitten, it gave way nicely to allow the very tender innards to meet the tongue, disclosing its softness and interesting spice.  It was the surprise star of the plate.  The mustard kicked up the flavor, but did not overwhelm the essence of the sausage.    We had the Stuffed Cabbage and Breaded Chicken Cutlet as our entries.  The Cabbage dish came with Mashed Potato and Cucumber Salad.  The Cabbage was tender and the mix of beef and something else was good, but perhaps a little bland.  It needed something to sweeten it, or at least that was how my -Jewish grandmother prepared them. The potatoes were not hot enough, and seemed to have been plated before visiting the oven. Mild disappointment.  The Cucumber Salad was a cream base and decent.    My Chicken dish was excellent.  The breast was large, with a pleasantly hand dipped breading coating it.  I opted for Mushrooms rather than Tomato Sauce, and was very pleased with the freshness and amount piled on the chicken.  Very tasty and definitely something I would order again.  The mashed were again cool and I left most of them alone.  The Red Beet Salad finished the plate.  Served appropriately cold, it was a nice fit, bringing mild sweetness to the mix of flavors in the breading, chicken, and shrooms.  I was happy.  To complete the repast, we ordered the Blintzes stuffed with 's Cheese, and dusted with Powdered Sugar.  These babies were wonderful.  Perfect crepe wrap, and a whipped sweet cheesy filling.  Light, and a perfect end to the meal with freshly brewed coffee.    This is a one of a kind richly local ethnic urban place that is easy to love.  The entire experience from the sidewalk scene, to the liquor store, to the special charm of the owner/chef, make  worth a visit or two.  When a meal becomes the food for a short story you have found something remarkable.   This was definitely that, and more.

Sedition is conduct that encourages acts of rebellion against the state. If a failure it is a serious crime; if successful, an act of revolutionary heroism. In times like these that try the souls of patriots, when it is difficult to differentiate between the criminals and the righteous, it is understandable that a subterranean public house would choose "Sedition" as its identity. No doubt the dark bricked, grottoed, underground tavern evokes an epoch when such weighty matters were discussed in hushed tones by serious people.   Chose a side or stand aside, but at least here you can do so with quality drinks and kitchen. We stopped in after visiting Penn Med a few blocks away. The basement felt cool in the dim light of reimagined industrial fixtures. We walked through coved rooms until taking a booth rather far from the bar. Yet, the friendly bartender found us with menus in hand. There were good beer choices, but having to return to see the medical staff after lunch, our libations were strictly water. We ordered the Philbano and Beer Braised Brisket sandwiches, and settled in.   Both were very good, as were the accompanying fries. The "Philly Cubano" was made up of smoked  pork butt, provolone, peach BBQ sauce and pickled long hots, all stuffed into a fresh Parker House roll. Simply put, it was a great pulled pork sammy. The combination of ingredients played well together and it was fun to identify the flavors as they announced themselves to the tongue.  First rate. The brisket was not quite as entertaining, but was tender and slathered in horseradish and coleslaw between the semi spheres of a brioche bun. Satisfying. Both were substantial enough to bring half home.   Whether you intend on sedition or will wait the next act out from the sidelines, be sure to enjoy life and stop in to Sedition for drinks and grub before deciding.

It's great to have a high end  pizza house in !  It's even better that the enterprise is owned by  and , the proprietors of , the excellent casa Italiana right down the street. This shop is for the daughter and son-in-law.  Thus, begin empires.   The building is on the site of the former Minuteman Press.  That old structure was taken down to the foundation, and a new Euro-Country Casual establishment arose.  Attention to detail is obvious, as the space is beautiful, with quality stone, wood, glass and a "just off the boat" wood burning hive oven covered in red glazed tile and contrasting white ceramic lettering that shouts, "Pasquale & Anna/Acqua e Farina!"    We were greeted by , the maestro , who sat my son and I at the corner table where we could see the whole operation.  We ordered a Siciliana pie, and as we waited, other servers brought thin slices of red sauced bread, and a small plate of Brussel sprouts that were soft and delicious from their time swimming in olive oil and spices.  I was even offered a glass of red wine on the house. Very cool touch!  The pie arrived with steam shimmering above it, on a large white platter.  It was cut in quarters, and covered in mozza, afterburn peccorino and chunks of eggplant.  Truly, a work of art with the bubbled crust and scorched undercarriage.  The special deal with these ovens is that they hold extremely high heat, such that the raw pie is placed in the oven for , while baking everything quickly and capturing all the flavor of the ingredients before they burn off and escape. The result is a wonderfully textured and tasty crust that is flavored by the ingredients you choose.  It is all about the dough (thus, the name, Water & Flour), and secondarily about the toppings.  Quite different than the better known pizza experience provided by most joints.   So it was here. A beauty to behold, and a pleasure to consume.  Of course, there is a downside to this approach to baking.  While the crust is excellent, the more ingredients you put on top, the wetter the center of the pie will be on the plate, because it is not possible to fully cook the veggies and meats in such a short time, and as a result of the lack of evaporation in the oven, the finished product will be softer that normal, and the drip from the collected moisture under the hood will be noticeable, and require care to avoid making a mess.   The secret is to order a simple pie with minimal topside accessories, so that the crust, cheese and sauce have the maximum opportunity to vent off the moisture.  This provides a drier bottom and optimal crustiness.   Dining at Acqua & Farina is very different than eating at pizza parlors.  It is designed as a feast for the senses.  There are more moving parts, and the resulting cost enhancement is noticeable. There is a time when "two slices and a soda," is what you want, but there are also times when although you yearn for pizza, you want a more rousing experience.    At those moments,  will be calling your name.

The Indiana Medical History Museum is a worthwhile field trip for anyone interested in history, medicine, psychiatry, and, to some extent, the macabre.  On the site of what used to be an 160 acre campus that housed 2000 patients with a variety of "mental illness", very few of the buildings escaped the wrecking ball.  Now, the tour concentrates on  which was the center for instruction as well as supporting the testing and autopsy of the patients on campus.      Tours start .  Because there is limited volunteer staff available, the doors are locked between tours. So plan on arriving  before the start of each hour or you will have to wait outside.  I am not sure if they can take credit cards, so plan on having $10 per adult on your tour.  Know that this isn't something for juveniles since most items are not to be handled.  Cameras are welcome, but the tour guide will tell you about places where cameras are not allowed due to privacy of the former patients' records.    After a brief wait, our group proceeded into the Amphitheater.  This large room served as both a lecture hall and taught through the autopsies performed in the spot where the lecturer would stand.  Students from the Indiana Medical College and from the Central College of Physicians and Surgeons received instruction.  In , these two schools merged with the Ft Wayne College of Medicine and the IU School of Medicine.  By , the autopsies were no longer conducted in the large room since the spread of tuberculosis affected nearly all of the physicians doing the autopsies and contaminated those who sat close to the dissection table.      Of interest in the Amphitheater is the original ice fed water fountain so that the lecturers would be able to get a drink.  Note that students were not allowed to have a drink from the fountain.  A large block of ice was loaded into a cabinet on the back side of the wall and as it melted, made fresh water available in the lecture room.    The next stop on the tour led to the smaller autopsy room.  A smaller room at the entrance held a "body cooler" while the surgeon prepared for the autopsy.  The larger room was sparse for easier cleanup and contained a metal table, a floor drain, weight scales, and a speaking tube where the surgeon performing the autopsy could speak into and have another surgeon on the floor above transcribe the notes.  Each autopsy had four pages of documentation per corpse.    The autopsy room has become a bit of a storage room now.  In there now, you will find donated equipment like an iron lung for youths, an old wooden phyician's chair, assorted wheel chairs of , and an odd collection of items that children/people had swallowed and had to have surgery to remove.  In the drawer we viewed, there were mostly an array of buttons and safety pins.  Other drawers had a collection of just about anything small enough to be swallowed.     The next room was the Anatomical Museum where a number of glass jars housed sections of brain traumas and abmormalities.  We were given time to wander through the exhibits and ask questions.  Of note was a "Brain-Slicing Machine".  Wow!  Another point of interest were a student's project of removing an actual nerve system from the spinal cord down to the fingers.  At first, it looked like a sideways tree, but upon closer examination, I could see it was real and had small labels identifying where the nerve sensations would originate.      The tour advanced more quickly through the remaining rooms.  On the rest of the first floor, there was a Chemical Storage Room, a Bacteriology Laboratory, and a reception area. The story of how syphilis was treated before the discovery of penicillin was discussed.  Syphilis' third stage could lead to insanity, so there were many patients on campus who were there due to this disease. Tests were developed there to help physicians identify the disease.  Early treatments included giving Mercury to patients.  That was replaced by Arsenic!  One of the last treatments before  the availability of penicillin was to infect the patients with malaria where the extreme fever would kill off the STD in about 30% of the patients.      The upstairs (sorry, no elevators available) houses the library, Histology Laboratory (microscopic tissue study), Clinical Chemistry lab,  lab, and patient records (where the autopsies were recorded from dictation below.)  In these rooms you will hear stories about advances in patient care and perception.  Mental patients were often shackled or kept drunk in  of treatment in order to manage their behavior.  Eventually, knowledge and acceptance that these illnesses could be treated and that patients should not lose their dignity and rights as humans prevailed.    The tour lasted .  In , the tour expands to include the former morgue (repurposed as a 's doctor's office) and an herbal garden.  Review #212

But considering some was taken home for dinner and the pastries (what didn't get devoured immediately) would be nice for breakfast !  It's multiple meals unless you are just a beast that stuffs yourself each meal.  Everything we tried was unique (other than the almond croissants), so in a time when I've become bored with my own cooking, it was fun to get out and try some new flavor combinations. Just take College north to 11th and be patient going passed the  construction.  Review #3784

I've picked up food from JC Teriyaki  in a row to try a few of their main dishes to see what was happening there. JCT sits on  just north of  in a somewhat rundown retail strip center which also has a  takeout joint and an  pizzeria. Nice to have options. It's Pizza Hut, we had a coupon. I have no excuses.  They had a special offer, a large 3 Topping Pizza and an 8 piece order of chicken wings for $16.99. We went with traditional in buffalo sauce.   Since we live in a neighborhood that has so many pizza joints within driving distance, I always opt for carryout. I may have to get out of the house and drive, but I get my food faster. When we arrived here, outside the employee door some of the employees were experiencing some, "sister drama". Their loud voices, spurting out profanities is not the first thing a new customer wants to see and hear.   Once inside the counter staff was friendly and very helpful. At this time we noticed different levels of hotness for the buffalo wings. We quickly asked which level we ordered and they said the hottest. Again, quickly we asked if ours had not been sauced if we could drop it a notch. Ours had been tossed, but they had an order after ours that had not. They quickly tossed them in the next level down and gave the next order ours. Talk about perfect timing.   I liked that when they brought our pizza out, that they lifted the lid to show us our order. For me that is taking customer service to the next level.   Once home, the wings were a sad excuse of chicken wings. They were tiny, tiny. If I didn't know better, I swear they were from baby chicks because they were that small.  The sauce was bland, perhaps we should have stuck with the Extreme. The pizza was just okay. I did like the way they chopped the green pepper and onion. They were larger pieces and not diced like so many other pizza joints.  I'm still miffed that they didn't have hand tossed crust.

Some things just make sense.  You want good steak?  Go to a steak house.  You want a good burger?  Go to a burger place.  (I hate reviews that order some obscure menu item and then complain that it wasn't the best they had ever had.  Really???)  So it seems to make sense that if you are a meat eater, but want to try something Vegan, then go to a place that specializes in Vegan foods and has a lot of options for you to try.  That was the case for my visit to Three Carrots' new sit down restaurant on , on  side of the interstate overpass.  My visit came during  and the sign wasn't even up on the outside and the roof was being worked on.  It may not look open if you drive by, but trust me, it is and ready to serve!  So, after finding free street parking, I entered into the newly refurbished building.  The interior was a mixture of artistic ceiling lanterns and art work with bare concrete floors and unadorned tables.  There were a number of two-top and some longer tables, and in the back on the left side, some bar stool seating.  I was greeted promptly and sat at one of the two-tops.  The waitress brought me a menu of lunch items as well as beverages (including alcoholic types) to choose from.    Being curious and having had little exposure to Vegan cuisine, I thought it best to order something that had meat and dairy counterparts out in the restaurant world.  I started with the "Mac and Cheese Croquettes" and then ordered the "Seitanderloin" as my sandwich.  The croquettes are made from what looks like mac and cheese, then rolled in breading, and deep fried.  I got five croquettes, somewhere between the sizes of golf balls and tennis balls, and my choice of BBQ or  sauce.  Too big for even my big mouth, I cut each croquette and dipped them into the sauce.  Wow!  Very nice texture and flavor.  The BBQ sauce had a little bit of heat (mostly in the aftertaste) and really complemented the M&C.  I still don't know what binding agent they use instead of cheese, but whatever it was, it did a fair job of looking like cheese and mostly held the croquette together.  Note that once you break the outer breading, there is enough moisture inside that the noodles may not stay in place.  At least they weren't dry and pasty, so chasing a stray noodle wasn't too much to accept.  Moving on to the sandwich, it also did a fair job of taking on the look of a breaded tenderloin, even extending beyond the bun as all good tenderloins do!  The sandwich comes impaled with a steak knife for those who like to slice their sandwich in half.  Here I encountered one of the negatives.  The "meat" part of the sandwich was a bit overcooked and made slicing through the sandwich neatly a bit difficult.  The sandwich also comes stacked with tomatoes, lettuce, red onion, mustard, and garlic aioli, and maybe some pickle (I don't recall seeing them, but they are listed on the menu.)  I ended up toppling my sandwich halves during the carving, but quickly reassembled the halves and took my first bite.... and I liked it!  The bit of overcooking made for a delightful crunch which my teeth had no trouble cutting through.  The flavor was very similar to a seasoned breaded tenderloin and provided a satisfying chew.  (I've had an under cooked bean burger elsewhere before and it fell apart, so I recommend erring on the side of crispy, not soggy.)    The sandwich also came with blue chips and salsa on the side.  The chips were crisp and the salsa a bit tangy, but served in a very small round dish.  Since the salsa was not thick, it tended to fall off the pointed end of the chips.  I ended up breaking my chips into smaller pieces to better scoop out more salsa.  Hopefully, the mgmt will figure out a better way to make salsa dipping easier.  Service was friendly, welcoming, and prompt.  Water was iced in pitchers and was topped off during my meal.  Noise level was moderate with a mixture of music styles playing over the speakers.  Overall, even if you aren't a Vegan, they have very approachable options that are available if you want to expand your palate exposure.  I did, and I liked it!  Review #461

Capital Health's new medical center in , , follows the trend in modern healthcare to merge the concepts of hospitals and hotels into a one stop shop for all medical needs, with a level of comfort and service that blurs the line between the two industries. Thinking of it as a hotel providing for health needs is probably accurate.   This is both good and bad. No one complains when a facility is clean, well staffed and meets the needs of everyone walking through the front door. The menu of services is extensive, with well trained professionals all around. Yet, the cost associated with these offerings can be excessive, and even with some insurance, beyond the financial means of most people. Those insurers have become more severe in their rejection of most invoices, realizing they are being asked to pay for a level of comfort for patients and visitors previously unavailable. What do you do when the hospital provides only private rooms and your carrier contracted with you to pay only a percentage of the semi-private rate? You hope you aren't admitted.   The level of specialization in each sub-discipline means a higher trained doctor is at your call, but while that is critical for some conditions, it is not for others. Still, the expense of over treatment is spread among all the patients without notice, nor consultation.   Part of this built in excess is due to how medical centers are developed, and the amazing tax advantages a health facility developer has over regular commercial work. The developer makes its money as the construction is done, while the management arm of the business can only expect pay as you go. Medicare, Medicaid and private insurers continually cut their portion of the bills to be paid, while the price tag on the service constantly goes higher. No wonder even the wealthy fear unanticipated medical expenses.   So, you have to hope the best medicine is available when needed, but also understand the cost of readiness and proximity may break your budget.

I had set up and bookmarked Pomodoro when I first read that it was to become the latest restaurant to make a go of it inside the first floor of  across from . There was a lot of cheese (three types) and ground beef and Pomodoro sauce.  So there wasn't a lot of flavor from either the meat or the sauce.  Maybe that is more authentic, but I found it rather bland.    After , my wife had finished her large bowl of salad and I was nearly finished with my meal when we flagged down the server to ask about the pizza.  He went back to the kitchen and then didn't follow up with us.  Instead, he seemed focused on the large party that had arrived in the back.  We then flagged down the second staff member who we met at the desk and let him know.  Again, he disappeared and didn't get back to us.    Finally, we got the attention of the first server and he went back and got my wife's meal.  Surprisingly, the 4 slices of pizza and another salad arrived on the same plate.  He said that the system had not delivered the food order to the kitchen which had caused the delay.  Seems odd that my order and a large salad got to the kitchen, but hers didn't.  Obviously, by this time, my wife was disappointed by the lack of follow up by the two staff members.  To make up for it, the server did comp her meal and gave her some complementary tickets towards future purchases.  But she was not a fan of the pizza which was a bit greasy from the pepperoni and somewhat limp/floppy in the middle (she prefers a crisper crust.)  And the pepperoni slices were not evenly distributed so that numerous bites were just cheese.    I understand that there can be some glitches in service at a new restaurant, but when a customer has to try three times to get someone to check on a meal, that is a basic mistake that needs to be addressed immediately.  I appreciate that the server tried to make amends but the difference of failing to give us feedback on the first request instead of the third makes it impossible for me to give this place a higher rating. This red colored ale had hint of tartness at the start and ended with a nice cherry flavored finish.  Very pleasant.  I moved on to the Working Girl Belgian Blonde (5.6%, 26).  This was the first I sampled with the flatbread and it went quite well.  I am a fan of  hops, so this was another pleasing choice for me.  My final selection was the BaconFace Brown (6.0%, ).  This was a very solid brown ale, but I was a bit disappointed that I couldn't taste any notes of bacon.  Maybe it was because I had begun eating, but my taste buds were just not able to taste much other than the basic brown ale.  Okay, but not up to the expectation of a name like BaconFace.   So, overall, I was glad to sample so many pleasant drinks in one flight and look forward to my next visit where I can explore some of the dark and bitter options.  I hope that they can eventually upgrade to glass drinking vessels from the plastic cups used in my flight.  Something about the plastic seems to signal a cheaper product than the fine quality I tasted.    Review #499

I stopped by for lunch and ordered a couple slices and an order of breadsticks.  The slices are huge (1/6th of a 20" pizza = 10" long and about 9" across!)  They have the pizza slices sitting out for you to select the type and then they do a quick reheat in the ovens to make sure it is warm when served.    After prepaying, I grabbed a seat in the dining room which looks bigger and cleaner than on my previous visit .  It probably isn't any bigger, but it felt like there was plenty of room.  Before long, my order was ready and I went back to the counter to pick it up.  I grabbed some napkins and utensils in case I needed them from a counter to the left of the order window.  They also have a beverage dispenser to the right.  The slices were served individually on their own plates.  I started with a supreme pizza that I believe they call .  It comes with pepperoni, mushrooms, olives, onions and peppers.  After a quick dabbing with my napkin to get the excess grease from the top, I noticed the the green peppers and the onions were in large clumps.  The cook had sliced them, but not all the way across, so I had to manually separate the pieces and spread them across the pizza so that I could have some in each bite.  And when I tried to lift the pizza to eat it, the center was so soft that it drooped and spilled the topping onto the plate.  I understand they may want their pizza slices to be folded, but this was just soggy and disappointing.  Fortunately, the flavor was good.  If they could just crisp the crust a bit before so that centers got done, it would improve the customer satisfaction a star or two!  I moved on to the sausage and pepperoni slice and it was in better shape, but still had a lot of grease on top.  I guess I should have left it since the sausage was so mild that it barely had any flavor.  The pepperoni were okay and the crust had a nice crispness to the bite while still being able to fold it.    It is sad that a local restaurant can't get the consistency down so that customers want to keep coming back.  As it was served, the pizza wasn't any better than a reheated frozen pizza I can get at the store.  Sure, the portions are generous, but I will pay for better quality if I can count on it.  Review #

I had no idea what to expect from Green Goddess when a friend told me that we had to try this place. After a decent walk through  and after being led down an alley, we were here. The bacon and salt added the perfect compliment to the sweet of the ice cream. It was a delicious combination, and definitely enough to make me want to go back and get this again.  All in all, I liked my meal here. I'd love to go back, but I will probably wait for autumn to do so.

Cheeseboro's Kitchen is a stand alone building on  that does soul food and other  classics.  It is primarily a take away house, with only a few tables along the front window for those who want to eat right there.  Ordering is done at the cash register, and each meal is prepared individually. The finished dishes come out on the other side of the room in front of the pizza ovens left over by the previous tenant.    The good thing about this approach is that the meals are hot and fresh.  Only the side dishes were premade and chilled as they wait for you.  The down side of this "just in time" production is that when they get busy, the wait can be rather long for your meal to be completed and brought out of the kitchen. Some customers call ahead, which while a good idea, just prolongs the wait for everyone.   The people working here, including management, are friendly and appear to be working hard to get the food out.  My questions were answered with a smile, even when I was showing my cultural ignorance about how certain things would be presented.  For example, a "sandwich" is not something between two slices of bread, but instead is a load of whatever you want on top of three slices of white bread.  You can make a sandwich of it yourself, but there is way more meat, fish, etc., than can fit within the confines of a manageable sandwich. Easier just to eat the food and as much of the loaf as you desire. Me? I skipped it all together in order to consume as much fish as possible.  Happy to be enlightened.   What about my whiting sandwich and side of macaroni salad (recommended)?  Six large fillets, light breading and flash deep fried, made for a delicious lunch.  I could only eat four of them. The macaroni side came in a plastic tub, mixed with copious mayo and bits of tuna.  Cool and great tasting. Again, more than this man could stuff down.    The only drawback to Cheeseboro's is the wait for the food to be prepared, and secondarily to the unused space in the store that could be put to use with more tables or perhaps, displays.  The meal, with the side and bottle of iced tea, came to around $12.  Quite reasonable for the quantity and quality of the offerings.  Now that I have a better idea what is going on, I will be back to try the rib sandwich, and perhaps, even their burgers, and more of their side dishes.

This quirky grouping of bronze sculptures is actually 3 sculptures that were on the site during the  Art Strategies public art promotion with sculptor .  Back then, 25 bronze sculptures were placed primarily along public ways in downtown .  The Otterness collection was one of the first of several annual public art initiatives sponsored in Indy.  The largest of the three sculptures is titled "Free Money" and was sculpted in .  The dimensions are 107.5 x 69.5 x 84 inches.  I wonder how many tourists observe that the base of the statue is a bag of money?  The smallest of the sculptures is titled "Male Tourist" from .  Its dimensions are 27 x 21 x 10 inches.  The male is left holding the bags for a third sculpture.  The third piece is titled "Female Tourist" and is a slightly taller figure taking a photograph, apparently of the "Free Money" sculpture.  The third figure is 34 x 16 x 14 inches.  If you look closely at one of the attached photos, you can see the spot where the third figure stood before being removed due to an act of theft/vandalism.  However, the statue is restored and completes the three pieces again.  What impressed me the most about the collection when it was in town was that the figures often appeared benign, almost childlike at first glance.  However, several made dramatic social commentary.  My favorite was "Big Big Penny" which was located on the steps of the War Memorial along with "Educating the Rich on Globe" and "Miser".  I recall having several interesting discussions as people stopped by and began noticing the details of the sculpture and how they related to the role of money, power, and the social classes. If you like your food with a bit of spicy heat, why not try a Flamme Burger!  I was able to find a spot in the busy parking lot outside the restaurant and once I entered, the hostess/manager (?) suggested I sit wherever I liked and she would follow with a menu and place setting.  I chose the dining area over the bar which was surprisingly full at lunch time.  I was greeted by my waitress and after getting my beverage, she took my order for the Flamme Burger and an upgraded fry option, the Truffle Parmesan Fries.  Although they offer a number of dips and aiolis for the fries, I chose not to add any since I wasn't sure what would go with the upgrade I selected.  While waiting, the servers came around to all the tables and passed out fresh baked chocolate chip cookies!  Not sure why since I didn't see them on the menu, but it was a nice surprise while waiting for my meal.    Before long, the burger came out first and then the fries . Not that big a deal since I was by myself, but not what I would normally expect at a restaurant.  The burger came on my choice of bun (whole grain for me) and was served with a steak knife to facilitate cutting it in half.  I ordered the burger medium per the recommendation of the hostess.  The burger (I'm guessing 6 oz) was a bit pink in the middle, but did have a good char on the outside from the cooking over flam(m)e, so it was moist/juicy but had that nice grilled flavor.  The burger came with a gruyere cheese and applewood bacon, and also was topped with serrano peppers and "flamme sauce" which is like a siracha mayo (I think).  So, with the multi layered flavor, there was a steady build up of spicy heat.  I didn't think it got too hot, but it was definitely noticeable.  Very tasty!  The fries were very plentiful and served in a paper lined metal basket.  I could see the bits of parmesan sprinkled generously over the fries throughout the mix, not just on the top.  However, the fries were a bit on the wilted/soggy side.  Maybe they didn't let the truffle oil get quite hot enough to give a crispness to the fries, but for some reason, the texture was a bit disappointing.  The flavor was very nice and I didn't think I needed any sauce.  Note that if you eat fries with your fingers, you will probably get parmesan bits on your finger tips, so be aware of that so you don't accidentally touch your clothes.  The service was friendly and thorough, with refreshed water and check processing as well.  Overall, a fine meal that was different from most burger places and tasty enough to warrant the premium burger prices.  I would gladly return if I was in the area.  Review #2185

The atmosphere of the farmers market is entertaining with all the / vendors dressed in their traditional garb and speaking colloquially. That is certainly worth the premium paid, as it is the only place in town where there is a real cultural exchange. Admittedly, Dos Amores lacks the   accent, but their  makes up for that.   I really should come here more often just to step away from modern times for a little while and enjoy all the interesting grub.

Let me regress for a moment, and talk about our salads.  More importantly the dressing. Their house dressing is , which is the off spring a Caesar and Mayfair. In my book, Moonlight has the best fried chicken, period.

If you are looking for something COMPLETELY different than your ordinary  Experience, The Vault of Souls is it.   This is -not- your daughter's theme park experience, this is an  experience that you won't find anywhere else.  of fear.  Don't come with the expectation of lines, of others body to body with you as you're herded though some chintzy maze, because that is not here.   What IS here? When your number is called, you will be brought down to the Vault, here you will be given a choice of which path to choose, and that choice is WHOLLY up to you. This is a nonlinear event. Each vignette is special, there are spirits in each room that will speak with you or not. They will interact with you in a different way. Your goal, to find the way out. It may take you as little as 20 minutes to get out, if you just briefly look things over, but it can take  if you thoroughly investigate and immerse yourself, and this is something you DO want to immerse yourself in. When you do find your way out, you can wind down a bit in the Gin joint, enjoy the music and dancers that perform for you, and of course the delectable libations. A couple of things to note: the event starts at $100.00 per ticket, and goes up to $400.00 Each ticket tier has it's benefits, and it is reservation only.   HOWEVER Each ticket comes with valet parking - in downtown , this benefit alone is amazing.  There is a dress code, Please don't come dressed in sneaks and a Tee, Come dressed to be immersed in the event, as if you were going out to the theater, Just, Please Ladies, no High Heels. The vault contains uneven floors, so spike heels are not suggested. The event is for 18+ and up, no children will be allowed.   -YOU- will be wearing the masks and asked to not speak while in the vault, this is so that the spirits do not follow you home.   Come enjoy a night of paranormal fun, a night of elegant fear with a sinister twist. The spirits are expecting you.

This franchise recently expanded into this part of the world, and I finally found a convenient moment to check it out .  It is an attractive  house; clean, organized and designed equally for eat in or takeout.  Yet, not an  in sight to speak to authenticity.  The options are set behind glass shielded steam tables, where the workers allow you to select from the number of different dishes offered, and spoon them onto a heavy cardboard plate with a side of white or fried rice.  As everything is prepared beforehand,  unless you arrive soon after wokking, the food cools and congeals to some extent, detracting from its overall taste and enjoyment. I went for orange chicken and  beef with the fried rice.  Both had a good look with different shades of orange and red amber goopy sauce.  The taste of each was distinct, and I believe that if hot, they would have been a satisfying meal.  Unfortunately, that was not the case. Both were barely above room temperature when I sat down, and although I appreciated the flavor and textural potential, the heat issue really drove down my enjoyment.  I don't know how they can fix this problem. I don't like micro-reheats, and question whether they could successfully throw it back in a wok.    So, I give them credit for an interesting idea, and a tidy house, but just don't want past prime hanging around food as part of my diet.

On the contrary, the seven items I sampled were all full flavored and moist, with enough spices to let you know this was , but mixed with enough familiar flavors that my palate was able to relate to it.    The staff out front was friendly, but did have a heavy accent which I struggled with understanding.  So even though I repeated my question about my dining options at lunch time, I am sure I looked like a deer in the headlights upon hearing his answer.  I decided to go with sampling the buffet, but I wasn't given much direction about how to proceed.       I wasn't sure if I was supposed to wait at my table or simply grab a tray and start helping myself (I helped myself like the other newbies ahead of me).  I could see staff milling about behind the buffet line, so I wasn't sure if I was supposed to have them serve me or use the spoons myself (I served myself).  I did find it awkward having to bend over to reach beyond the wall to clear the low overhang.  I could see most customers were expressing some concern about reaching over the hot trays to spoon foods from the second row of entrees.  It was interesting to hear the comments as I sat at the table nearest the food line.  It was easy to tell first time customers from regulars.  I also didn't get a bill when I finished, so I walked up to the counter and initiated the payment process.     And that is the difference between running a restaurant and a food truck.  Expectations are higher at restaurants when it comes to service and for folks who are new to a restaurant, having someone work the front dining area who can clearly direct customers is a must.    Review #347

St. Louis Union Station Soda Fountain is the perfect spot to have a quick lunch/bite before or after riding, The St. Louis Wheel.   Our party of three arrived at  and there already was a wait for tables. Over half the restaurant was filled with convention attendees. It was easy to spot them, they all had lanyards hanging around their necks.  Even with the crowd, our wait was not long.   Normally, I like the coziness of a booth, but  we were seated at a four-top table in front of the actual soda fountain. It was a great show, it was fun watching the, to use a classic term, "soda jerks" make all the sweet treats. Numerous times we were asking our server, "what's that?". They all looked so delicious. For our sweet treat, after our lunch we ended up enjoying, The King.   Now let's talk about the real reason we came here, our lunch before riding The Wheel. I ordered the Single Grilled Cheeseburger and my cousins enjoyed, Fried Chicken Sandwich and a BLT. To accompany our sammies, we all shared two sides; Crinkle Fries and Onion Rings.   I enjoyed my burger, which was loaded up with the typical, LTOP. A single was enough, I could not imagine eating a double along with a side and one of the sweet treats. My cuz who had the Fried Chicken Sandwich said it crisp, moist and flavorful. She normally doesn't like mayo and had them put it on the side. When it arrived, it was a flavored mayo in a little cup and she liked it. Her husband, enjoyed the BLT. He said the applewood smoked bacon was a flavorful twist on the classic sandwich.   We were so glad we all shared the our sides. The portions are plentiful and enough to share. The crinkle fries (my favorite style) were crispy and seasoned with just enough salt. The onion rings I found out are not made it house, but I'll tell you that they were pretty tasty for being a frozen product. It could have fooled me, they were that good.   The dessert, our finale was a delicious sweet treat. As I stated earlier, we went with, The King. It was a delightful mix of sweet and salty. It all centered around a big scoop of peanut butter banana ice cream, surrounded by sliced bananas and covered in peanut butter sauce, topped with bacon and chopped peanuts. A sundae is not complete without the whipped cream topping and maraschino cherries on top.    our server was a delight. He was honest with his recommendations and didn't mind splitting our checks and that we shared our sides and dessert. I was also impressed that one of the managers was hands on assisting all the servers. She even took time out twice to chat with us about our first visit. The floor captain also came over and thanked us for coming in as we were getting ready to leave. Overall, very friendly staff.   When: ,  Why:  before riding, The Wheel

Their server did a great job of waiting on the tables and serving the bar, she is trained well. By that, I mean she is trained like 's dog. She commented that she never thought of that, but it was so true.   I am a new fan of The Mack and it is being added to 3 of my lists; Burgers, Wings and Eco-Friendly.

I went to see my first movie at a cinema in a long time as the pandemic is stabilizing. I made it okay, but it definitely crossed my mind that an improvement could be made.     My wife bought tickets and thought our seats would be higher  even though the tickets said row B. (Probably where we should have grabbed our seats) but it seems odd that they use the same row name for two different rows. In what seems like , ,  and I made plans to dine at .  Our wait was finally over on a blustery , when we descended upon .  The restaurant was full but for one table when we arrived around 8:30. We shared an orange scented flan, a pumpkin cheesecake that had the most wonderful crust and a delicious banoffee tart that  claimed the  were first responsible for creating.  Many props to our friends across the pond for that one!  The check arrived and with it came three house-made cocoa dusted truffles.  It was a beautiful ending to a fabulous meal.  As  mentioned, we were fortunate enough to catch a glimpse of the New Year's Eve prix fixe menu, and it sounded wonderful.  Do not hesitate to give Sycamore a try; it's a suburban gem and it won't be long before resies are hard to come by!
