Wow! What a cool experience right here in downtown Indy.  As a local, I've heard the  name for most of my life, but wasn't that familiar with the author's work until recently.  Having just read "Slaughterhouse Five" and a collection of short stories "Welcome to the Monkey House", I got an appreciation for how imaginative and engaging the author was.  The museum is open for visitors to view with three floors of items and artwork, a book store, and soon, a coffee shop.  But if you want to get your money's worth, contact the museum to find out when the guided tours ey make the experience so much better.  My tour guide was very knowledgeable and had a sense of wit that complemented the author's.  The museum has several sections which are interesting for different reasons.  One section has a collection of banned books and I just can't get over that some narrow minded communities think that ideas can be shut down.  Hint:  There's a thing called the internet and people will get whatever they want, so don't be an * about it.  There are also books that are by authors that inspired  or fit into the styles of writing that the author liked.  Note that members of the museum can take advantage of the lending library here.  Up on the second floor is a gift/book shop where you can find items to purchase related to the author.  On the third floor, there was a Slaughterhouse Five exhibit that features a lot of text and imagery from the author's time as a prisoner of war after the Battle of the Bulge during WWII when he was forced to march to  and kept in an underground slaughterhouse.  Also of note is that if you go online at the station on the second floor, you will find a wide variety of information and images about  for you to explore.  For those who have trouble negotiating stairs, there is an elevator available.  I highly recommend this museum for adults who consider themselves free thinkers.  I don't think this is a place that children would appreciate simply because they probably won't have had enough life experience to understand the ideas and concepts the author wrote about.    Parking is free in the mini lot that surrounds the building with access off  as well as /MLK Blvd.   parking is also available on Indiana Ave.  The tour lasted  (mine started at )  Definitely worth checking out to get a fuller experience from the museum. The sauce was lick-the-plate worthy.  And for dessert one of the BEST classic creme brulee.  Lightly laced with Gran Marnier and a crispy top.  Service was very attentive UNTIL the end when we needed our check.  At  nearly everyone (there were several waitstaff) disappeared.  The Chef came out to our table prior to and during service and was collegial and utterly charming.  (Really.)  It helped that I speak  and was seating next to a lovely, fluent,  woman.  (Merci, Madame!)  Will I return?  Oh yes - but not in a hurry.  I would simply like to sit in the bar downstairs and have desserts off that AMAZING dessert cart (not part of our meal, alas).  That opera cake has my name on it!  !  Oh - and don't laugh but I actually drank (again don't laugh) a Mojito with my meal (I know, I know - in a  restaurant) and it was GREAT.  And it was $10.  My husbands  was $12.  They do not serve Veuve Cliquot - which was what I was jonesin' for.

WOW! I cannot tell you how excited I was waiting for the Copper Pig to open. Now that it has opened, I am sad to say, it is the winner of a Stevie B Yelp Award. Dish was overly salty. Good thing for the water girl.  4) Beet Fries - Tasteless. I love beets and these were flavorless mush. Disassembled sandwich to see if that would help, but it was the actual beef that was making it tough and chewy.  6) Board Burger - Mealy burger, with a grey tint. My friend said, it resembled a burger  from McDonald's. Her dog wouldn't even eat it when served the leftovers which were the majority of the burger. (Take note of photo) 7) Cocktails - Weak and unprofessionally prepared. Obvious their bartenders are more comfortable opening beer bottles and pour a draft beer. No skills in a well crafted cocktail.   After leaving  we went down the street to another establishment and ran into several other diners who where at the  as well. We all compared notes and were in agreement that they have a lot of improving to do.   I hate for a business in my hood to be on my Terrible Two's List. So I'm going to give them  to work their kinks out and hopefully they will. Then I'll revisit them again and hopefully be able to raise my rating.  When:  Why: Belated Birthday Dinner

The new distillery/brewery from  is open!  The building is spacious and has a lot of cool features to make the visitors happy.   First, despite the construction, you can get here from the east or west and park for free inside the new  (located on ).  Be careful of construction workers if you cross , but you can get through!  Second, there is a new plaza being built right in front of the building, so  has provided a nice sidewalk to skirt around the construction on the east side of where the plaza is going in.  That should add to the view of the location even more.  Next, the building is very cool.  Two stories of contemporary design with lots of wood (patterns on the walls, stairs, and a flag on the second floor) and lots of gray tones for a somewhat industrial look.  Note that this building doesn't look like a warehouse.  Also, a second floor patio is located on the west end of the building just outside of one of the bars.  Behind the second floor bar is a private room that can be reserved for parties.  Speaking of bars, there is one on each floor, both on the west end.  You can place your beverage orders directly at the bars and grab a seat there, or in one of the many seating areas.  However, you can also flag down one of the roving servers and they will take your beverage order and deliver it to you.  Each table top has a full menu of the liquors, the cocktails, the beers, and even a list of all the food items from each of the food vendors on site.  As far as food goes, three of the four food vendors were operating on .  On the main floor, Oca has a shop in the center of the building, beyond the staircase.  They sell food to eat and packaged items to take home.  Also on the first floor is La Margarita (from ) serving  dishes.  There is room for another restaurant to the right of La Margarita.  On the second floor, you can get pizza from Pi (which also has a food truck in Indy).    For all of the food vendors, you simply go to the counter, place your order and pay and then wait for your food.  I tried the personal sized pizza and only had to wait .  Note that you pay for food at the counters and the beverages on a separate bill unless you are getting a soda from the vendor.  I took advantage of the wait to select one of the cocktails on the menu:  the Matcha Bird which is made from a collaboration of Sun King and Cardinal with a Bird Royale Spirit, Matcha (tea), honey, passion fruit,  (bottled water) and Sumac Sugar.  It was delicious!  The server brought my drink to the second floor dining area I selected and the drink went well with the pizza.    The only negative beyond the construction is that the distillery is  away from producing their own line of liquors.  In the meantime, they have invited a number of local, state, and regional distilleries to collaborate on some liquors.  As the Sun King brands become available, they will eventually phase out the other items and go solo.  Some of the collaborations are in short supply and may not last long.    I really enjoyed my experience and was welcomed by the staff which encouraged me to browse around so that I could make up my mind.  I look forward to my next visit.  Review #1039

If you don't mind paying $23 for a four pack of local suds, Newtown Brewery is a worthwhile destination for the yeast heads in the crowd. The facility is very attractive with plenty of wood and stone, and the beer is excellent for the most part.   We stopped in  and the room was hopping. Tables full of folks escaping  captivity. But, we weren't ready for a space packed with over a hundred people without masks, nor social separation, so we bought our "I lost My Marbles"  Tripel four can and headed home. Just didn't feel safe (and thus the one star deduction for lack of public awareness by management).  Under better circumstances, Newtown Brewing would be a big hit in these parts, and in fact, it appears it already is.   The beer was quite strong at 11% alcohol content, but the taste was great, and the color a robust rusty slurry. Liked it a lot. I'm no expert, but these guys seem to have the right recipes.   They do have a food truck in the parking lot most weekends, and we were fortunate to approach the window of Stuff'd  and grab two sliders to partake with the ale at home. They were great and a perfect partner to the cold fermentation. More on them in a separate review coming soon to these Yelp pages.   I hate to have to take out a loan to support my occasional beer addiction, but aside from that, and the insensitivity to the CDC guidelines, Newtown Brewery really enhances the neighborhood. Just hope no one gets exposed to the virus. That is a price far to high to pay for a momentary pleasure.

I've had 's bookmarked for quit awhile, so when the BF said he wanted to go here for lunch I agreed. I'll disclose up front, I am not a Hot Dog eater. I wish they offered an old fashioned bun as an alternative for us old fuddy dud-dies.   Doing the Two Dog Combos did give us the opportunity to experience four different dogs. Selecting from the large (16) variety was hard, but we quickly narrowed it down.  's Famous Chili - Cheese,  Dog, Crazy Cajun Creole and Bacon - Bacon . All four had good presentation in their little red baskets and  is very generous with the toppings.   The Chili - Cheese was very messy and hard to hand handle. This one for sure, needs to be cut and eaten with a fork. The Chili had a good flavor and can easily stand on its own in a bow.   I like the fact that they smoke their own dogs and brats on site, we saw them at work as we approached the entrance. The STL - CHI Dog was a true ballpark frank. I could enjoy this one at a Cardinals and Cubs game. The only change I'd make is removal of the tomato,  I'm not a fan of tomatoes. I'd also reduce the amount of onions, to reduce the heartburn.   Bacon - Bacon Jamaican Dog, was a disappointment and it had two of my favorite things; bacon and pepper jack. The description said, two slices of bacon and I expected two slices, one of each side of my dog. Instead, it was chopped and on top.  However, the jerk seasoning and sweet chipotle sauce was a nice touch.   The winner of the four was the Crazy Cajun Creole. A locally smoked Andouille sausage with grilled onions, spicy brown mustard and  BBQ Sauce.  This one I could hand handle and enjoy, but still found the bun to be chewy.   If either of us return, I know we will go with simpler toppings. The ones we selected on this visit gave both us heartburn, indigestion and upset stomach. We must have delicate digestive systems.

What a fantastic little spot! Fellow  suggested that we try this place and since I had heard a lot of good things about it, I was down.  This cozy little restaurant on Tchoupitoulas is the perfect spot for  or a celebration. We made reservations for 8, and although we were , we were seated immediately upon arrival. We were given our menus and we ordered some wine. Looking over the menu, I immediately knew what I wanted. As a starter we decided to get the scallops, which were pan seared with butter, lemon, croutons and capers. My experiment paid off because these scallops were delicious. They were flavorful and I really liked them a lot. I really can't say enough about this part of the meal and I was beside myself happy.  Finally, we really decided to indulge and we treated ourselves to the chocolate mousse. This delicious concoction of whipped light chocolate came in a small chocolate shell bowl. The mousse was delectable and light and was the perfect conclusion to the meal. I also liked the presentation. I posted a picture- it really is a work of art.  The staff was very attentive the entire time and was quick to refill the wine glasses and clear the plates when necessary. I was really very pleased with the entire experience and I think that  might be one of my new favorite dinner spots in the city.  I would absolutely go back and I am now hungry for more catfish and grits.

I was doing some work at the mall and I was pretty much forced to eat here, because it's the only relatively healthy restaurant in the food court at .  I'm going to start by saying the food was good. As good as the food was, I found it a little pricey. The meal itself was $9.50 and my water was another $3 (even though it said water is $2 on their menu board). I just wish that the healthy option at the mall wasn't the most expensive, but I guess that's just the way things go. I wouldn't have a problem paying $9.50 for a wrap and a side salad at an actual restaurant, but I did find that a little steep for mall food and $3 for water is just insane.  I'm giving four stars because the food was fresh and service was fast, especially considering there was a line. I liked my wrap, but I probably wouldn't get it again because paying over $12 for a wrap, a pile of lettuce and some water makes me feel pretty dumb.

Note:  I only ate at the restaurant without shopping at the grocery.  I didn't realize until I started working on my review that there are Tiendo Morelos restaurants/markets all around town. Even though there is a counter at the cooking area, you don't order there. Apparently the cashier had a little trouble understanding me when I ordered the  and  tacos.  I was brought out the  and Lomo instead. (I was the only customer at the time.) The tacos were excellent.  They were served on double layered corn tortillas.  I usually prefer flour, but wasn't given an option here.   These were the best tasting corn tortilla shells I've had.  And the ingredients inside were delicious with the added items being colorfully fresh.    The side of beans and rice were forgettable.  Not bad, just lacking much texture and flavor.  Very bland and not much other than filler when compared to the robust flavor of the tacos.  The staff was friendly and the restaurant was pretty clean looking, so given the high quality of flavor, I would recommend stopping by to quench your  food cravings.  Review #2698

Parx Beer Garden is a recent addition to the Parx Casino complex in , . It is an indoor/outdoor facility with folding doors separating the large warehouse space from the attractive green garden area. Totally different and worth the experience.   I also give a thumbs up to the house salad and Bruschetta.  I've dined in and I've called ahead for carry-out and every time I have been pleased with my meals. I want this place to continue to succeed, so I recommend it to all pizza lovers. I just hope it doesn't get so popular that I cannot get in to enjoy one myself.

The BBQ taste was both sweet and tangy, just as it should be.  The Wings are larger than found in most outlets, but the hotness covers every nook and cranny.    I can't say that these items were the best I ever had, nor that they were as good as it gets.  Yet, given what is available in the area, they are all on the high end of taste and enjoyment, and for me, there is no need to look further afield to satisfy my Fried Chicken Addiction.   And, if you come on a  you can enjoy an impromptu car show in the parking lot.  Folks are there from all over opening their hoods and hooking up their stereos to external speakers so everyone can check out their wheels to .

When you first enter here you may say to yourself, "Where's the beef? Where's the pork?" What you need to do is stop and think. What is the name of this BBQ joint? So you'll soon forget that they do not offer beef brisket or pulled pork.    I would have never discovered GSS if it were not for  organizing a UYE lunch. My lunch was the Smoked Chicken Wings and they were Gobble-icious.  They were served drummette style and seasoned with their signature herbs and spices. They may have been slowly smoked, but I gobbled them up fast. I had the sauce served on the side, but was totally satisfied with the signature rub. As my side, I choose Green Beans which had pieces of ham. They were the perfect accompaniment to BBQ as they would be a  fried chicken.   I couldn't enjoy a new BBQ place without taking some home for the other half who was working in the yard. A Half Smoked Chicken with two sides would be the perfect reward. Another solid addition to the  dining choices arrived  at the former location of 's. They have a full service bar with a nice selection of drafts as well as a large number of bottled/canned craft beers.    I stopped in for lunch and started with the Crispy Brussels Sprouts. I stopped by on a chilly  for a late lunch after running errands in .  This place shares the building with a Family Video store on  corner of  property ( corner of  and ).    The signs out front and on the side mention sushi, but guess what.  They no longer have sushi on the menu and the waiter confirmed that they don't have it any longer.  So, scratch that from my selections.  I decided to go with a cup of Rangoon Tea/Coffee based on other Yelper suggestions and followed that with a bowl of Steak Noodle Pho.  The tea was served at a drinkable temperature and was surprisingly sweet!  I know I've tasted the underlying flavor before, but I'm unable to determine what it reminded me of.  Whatever it was, it was great.  (Note that a single cup was plenty for me.  I don't believe you get free refills.)  Before long, by large bowl of Pho arrived with a fork and  soup spoon (ceramic).  It also had a small plate with sliced pepper (looked like jalapeno), mint sprigs, and raw bean sprouts.  I also received bottles of Hoisin and  sauces.    I must admit I have had Pho three times previously and was clueless on what was proper.  So I You Tubed it and solved the problem.  I added the individual leaves off the mint, the sprouts, and the pepper slices and stirred them in, letting the hot broth semi-cook the new ingredients and let their flavor spread into the pho.    The broth was tasty even before I added the new ingredients, so I really enjoyed the perked up flavor.  At the bottom of the bowl, the long rice noodles (think white thin spaghetti) and the thin sliced beef nestled.  I think the owners realize that most Hoosiers would struggle using chopsticks to fish out noodles, so the fork was a welcome tool.  And whenever I speared a bit of the steak, I dipped it in the Hoisin sauce I had put on my small serving bowl that the soup spoon had been delivered in.  The steak (and probably all the meat options) don't have a lot of seasoning since they soak in the broth, so dipping the pieces directly in the Hoisin makes for a much tastier bite.  Yes, the meat gets a bit chewy, but because it is sliced thin, it wasn't difficult to get used to.  (I am not sure how the shrimp would hold up since I am not a fan of it when it gets rubbery.)  The dining room was pretty sparse, so the noise level was low even with some classic rock playing softly in the background.  Not much atmosphere inside, but the bright tangerine walls and a few decorative plates kept it from looking too sterile.  Overall, a good meal (huge quantity) and nice service all at an affordable price.   Now, if they would just take down those Sushi signs...  Review #2219

East Lincoln Highway, , , is primarily noted as the location of the Reedman-Toll automobile dealership, the largest car outlet in the country. In its shadow are many smaller businesses, including this Friendly's restaurant. Obviously, it is well known, as when I arrived  night, it was more than half full of customers chowing down on the traditional  cuisine and ice cream desserts for which this chain is known.   I was guided to a booth along the front wall by the hostess, and handed the laminated multi-paged menu. Their Sriracha Burger sounded interesting, and I went with it, medium. Unlike many burger joints that promise the desired degree of grilling, but inevitably deliver only a well done puck, this kitchen did keep its word. The rest of the accompaniment - pepper jack cheese, bacon, onion straws, lettuce, tomato, sriracha mayo, on brioche bun - were all present and accounted for, although the "crispy" onion was soggy. The overall taste satisfied my burger craving for . At ten bucks it was priced beyond its actual value, but it was good to know that Friendly's was keeping up with the burger wars, where every food emporium had to offer a decent six ouncer to stay competitive.   It is safe to say that Friendly's keeps up with the other franchise Joneses in this universe. You can come here for a burger or other of their beef and chicken offerings, and leave sated. And, if in the mood, their ice cream makes for a very convenient and creamy end of meal.   Looks like Friendly's will be around for a while longer.   3.5 STARS

If you are in the mood for a simple meal and want to support local, you may really like this place.  If you want a burger and don't want to pay over $12 for it, you may like this place too. So, since I hadn't been here in a long time, I thought I would see how the food and experience held up in my absence.  I remembered that they were packed before, so I decided to target  to avoid the lunch rush.  The parking lot was still full!  When I entered, I was a little surprised that there were plenty of seats at the bar or at one of the many tables inside.  There wasn't anyone greeting me at the door, so instead of standing there waiting, I headed over to the chairs at the bar.  (Note that the restaurant is for 21+, so they don't have to segregate the bar from the dining area with some faux railing/wall.)  Before long, I was greeted by the server behind the bar and after asking if I had been there before, she made sure to remind me that it was a "cash only" operation.  With that out of the way, I went with a simple single burger with cheese, ketchup, mustard, tomato, and lettuce and an order of fries on the side.  Before long, my plate was ready.  The burgers are small compared to most restaurants.  They are served very thin so they can get a crisp char on the edges (I like my burgers with a tasty browning to bring out the flavor.)  The toppings are also served inverted.  The tomato was on the bottom with shredded lettuce next, then the burger and melted cheese were next.  The problem here is that the cheese sticks to the bun, so the self serve condiments require lifting the cheese and burger off to apply the sauces.  Without lifting the burger, I wasn't sure if there were any condiments on the sandwich until I took a bite since the server hadn't mentioned they were self serve.  Overall, the burger was cooked nicely, but was under seasoned.  Yes, they do have salt and pepper shakers on the bar, but I'm simply stating that I have expectations that my food will be seasoned when delivered.    The fries were crisp on the outside and tender inside.  Very good!  But again, they were unseasoned.  I did add salt to them and used the ketchup bottle to add flavor.  No problems there.  Overall, it was a decent burger, maybe a bit unique in its presentation and preparation.  But honestly, I can make this meal at home without having to drive to the near west side.  And I don't have to worry about having enough cash.  Review #775

All reviews are in the end subjective.  Sometimes all the variables are evaluated, but in other instances one aspect so dominates that the other pieces are minimized by comparison. How many coffee mugs are found in Coffee Cup Café?    I'll never tell.

Maybe it's because I have visited  Café often enough over  to be its Duke, or maybe it's the way the owner of  establishment smiles at me when she sees me walk in, but the food here seems to be getting better.    The joint still looks every day of its longevity in , and sorely needs a makeover that brightens it up and takes the storage out of the dining room, and it wouldn't be the worse thing in the world if Mr.  trimmed his  beard.  Nonetheless, some kind of magic is happening in the kitchen that is creating more distinct and enjoyable dishes from the lunch menu.    , the Hot & Sour Soup took me by surprise. Whatever the reason, China Café has my appreciation, with sincere hope that it continues on this path.

I stopped in for lunch and Wow! What a great meal! Twenty Tap recently reopened and they must have been fine tuning their service and food prep the whole time they were going through the remodeling.  I had never been here before, but lured by the Yelp Top 50 designation (), I thought it worth the trip from the southwest of  to drive here.  First, know that there is no parking lot, so you need to find a spot on the street.  Mine was a couple blocks away.  There is a small front patio area (covered) for outdoor dining, but I wanted to see the inside and waited for the staff to find a table for me.  Service was prompt throughout my meal.  Water brought out, extra napkins and a bottle of ketchup delivered without asking, and quick turnaround on getting my bill at the end.  The wait on the food and drink were short too.  Like I said, good all around!  I started with a draft local () and got the full pint for $5.  That is less than I am used to for craft beer, so I counted that a win.  (The beer was cold and tasty too!)  I ordered the Short Rib Grilled Cheese sandwich with a side of seasoned fries.  YUM!  The sandwich, served on  toast, was one of the best I've had all year! The short rib meat was juicy and when paired with the smoked gouda and  cheese, made a winning combo.  The cheese was completely melted and gooey, so it held most of the ingredients together (although a bit of meat did drop a couple times.)  There was also a cherry bourbon glaze on the meat and a jalapeno marmalade along with the carmelized onion and arugula.  What surprised me was how sweet tasting the sandwich was.  The marmalade had just a hint of pepper flavor, not any detectable spiciness.   And the fries were so good!  I couldn't really tell what seasoning they used, but they reminded me of fries I've had that were cooked in Duck fat.  Almost buttery tasting while being crunchy crisp on the outside.  Nearly perfect fries!  Overall, a really positive first visit to this place.  Can't wait to return to try one of their house burgers!  Review #381

I was excited to try . I've heard about it in passing, so when a friend of mine got a couple's float through Groupon and invited me to come with, I jumped at the chance.   I'm acquainted with things in the Woo range, and this is most certainly there. The comfortable space of the reception area/sales floor is made more so by the warm energy of the varied crystals and jewelry up for sale. The small oxygen bar sits off to the side of the baroque red plush sofa.  Once we signed in, we were shown the bathroom/shower and instructed that when it was time, we'd come in and shower without soap. make sure to remove all oils on our skin. Then we'd go back to the individual pods, insert ear plugs and get in, closing the doors behind us.  Seemed easy.   We were shown the pods, these were rectangular, about 4.5' high, the same width, and 6'long, draped with a mandala. A little table to hold your personal items and a little box that holds the individually packaged earplug sets.  In one corner of the room was an infrared sauna that had jaunty lights - this is their sauna and light therapy offering.  Our host left and we proceeded to follow his directions, each of us careful to take a towel with us - One thing to note, the floors just outside of the shower, though there is an anti-slip pad, just beyond that, is very slippery, watch your step.   We each chose our pods and began our journeys. Here's what you need to know: The pods are filled with a water/Epsom salt /hydrogen peroxide solution. Some people may have issues with it, so keep this in mind please.  The water is comfortable upon getting in, it feels just above skin temperature, and as you settle in, you lose the difference between air and water. The air around you is close and warm as you slow your breathing and settle, letting yourself relax.  It is dark.. completely dark.  If you are claustrophobic, this might not work.  And with ear plugs in, all you have to focus on is your thoughts, your breath and your heartbeat.  It is very womb like.   My friend M, she said she fell asleep. I did not, but I did relax greatly. My body seemed to lengthen, to stretch. My shoulder which has been aching for a dog's age is feeling much better than it has. I did not have a spiritual experience, but I did have very clear thoughts.   When our time was up, our host came in and knocked on our pods and we got out slowly.  Keep in mind, you're covered with salt infused water, you will see this as soon as you hit the air.. since my friend was taking her shower first, the salt began to dry on me, which meant it began to itch.  Be thorough in rinsing your skin, don't forget your ears, you'll find salt in the oddest places.  If you want to, bring conditioner, soap and shampoo is provided (and they smell really nice!)   All in all a really nice experience, I would do this again in a heartbeat.

I have taken the guided tour of the stadium and been to events held at the stadium, both on the field and in the conference rooms below.  So, my overall impression is quite favorable.  There seems to be generally comfortable accommodations in the seating for the big events without feeling packed.  Sure, a little more room between rows would make it easier for attendees to get passed each other, but we seemed to manage okay.  Although an effort has been made to make signs to help attendees navigate this huge space, I did find it somewhat confusing when fortune made using the ramps necessary.  There seems to be signs for the ramp system that lead to dead ends or closed doors without electronic opening buttons to push.  That required coordination between the guest in the wheel chair and myself on navigating through the openings.  Seems like it was awkward in general and could be dangerous in an emergency.    I like that the stadium hosts events of many kinds including overflow for the convention system conveniently located next door.  There are some dining options available, but considering the large number of attendees for the events, you need to either eat before arriving or plan on allowing enough time to get through the lines.    Most of all, having the stadium opens the possibility for attending events that would not be possible if the facility were not here.  Accessible from each side of town, the location is perfect for those staying downtown during a convention. For those in the suburbs, traffic quickly disperses from the area, unlike many of the waterfront stadiums which force all the traffic in a single exit route.  As someone who used to be stuck in traffic on  in , this is infinitely better!  The tour that is provided at a low cost during  is informative and is generally held in groups small enough that allows for attendees to ask lots of questions.  The scale of the stadium is immense, especially when you stand on the field and look at the seating/roof area during the tour.  The engineering necessary for such a facility is mind boggling.  Overall, it is a stadium/facility that serves the community well.  Review #441

While on the east side of Indy, I decided to stop by for ice cream and ended up getting that AND dinner.  This colorful shop sits on the corner of  and English and has free parking around the building. The pressed bread takes on a chewy texture, but in a pleasant way.  The flavor was really good, though the juiciness made it something to watch out for since the juice had an orange color that looked like it could cause one heck of a stain.  Fortunately, they wrapped it in foil and then put it in a small plastic sleeve to catch the drippings.  I simply peeled back the foil and slid the sleeve down as I ate and managed to not spill a drop!  I still needed some napkins, but was relieved that I didn't have to do laundry when I got home!   The folks behind the counter were friendly and made the wait time seem minimal.  I appreciated their willingness to explain some of the terms that I was unfamiliar with. The husbeast and I wanted to try someplace new for dinner, so we went to what used to be "" and now it's , a pizza joint with a bar and other food. Our waiter,  was brand new and though he felt like he was stumbling over everything, he really wasn't. He was polite and helpful and very sweet.  We'll come back, to try something OTHER than the pizza, and pray the entertainment ISN'T the same lounge singer.

I'm tempted to give four stars, because I've never had a bad experience (besides the standard wait time for a table, of course), but something is holding me back... most likely, the extra weight I put on after my meal on . Woo wee.  I love this place!  They have so many neat things, from furniture to beer (different departments ;)).  This is the place to go to if you are looking for . I stopped by on  for lunch and although there was a nice sized crowd, I could get in the door (unlike !).  There is a small parking lot in front of the restaurant that is shared with the grocery and coffee shop.  It is a bit of a tight fit, so you may want to choose some street parking on the south side of the lot as a better option.  The restaurant is one that you may place your order at the counter (plastic menus are available to read or you may read from the overhead menu behind the counter.)  Once you pay, you are given a number to take to your table and they bring out your food when it is ready.  They ask you to be patient since it is not "fast food" despite looking like it.  No heat lamps here keeping things kinda hot until you order.  I ordered the Original burger (1/4# of pasture raised beef) with Mug sauce, American Cheese, LTOP, on a plain, soft bun.  I also went with the "Fresh-cut Fries".    The burger was thin and had a nice char without being dry.  I am not sure I can describe the Mug sauce flavor, but it was unique to my burger experience and a pleasant surprise.  I definitely recommend it.  The fries were generously portioned and had a crispy crunch.  The lard used in cooking adds a little flavor, but because the crunch layer is thick compared to the overall thickness of the fries, the potato flavor is muted.  The server asked if I wanted catsup and salt for the fries, but instead of a bottle and shaker, I was given a packet of each.  Sure, I could have grabbed more from a central display inside, but I would definitely prefer have bottles and shakers so that I didn't have to tear open a bunch of packets.  (Am I the only one who finds it odd that the place is promoting natural foods, but using lots of plastic and paper packets?)  Anyway, since I didn't grab any additional salt and catsup, the fries didn't have the flavor that I expected.  Note:  you can add toppings to your fries for more flavor for an upcharge  I noted garlic and pulled pork options while there.  The menu has desserts, beer, and wine available to go with their assorted sandwiches and sides.  The staff seemed positive and efficient.  The only negative is that a number of folks who were getting their food to go or waiting on others to join them tended to congregate in front of the counter.  (Maybe they should make some sort of line to help newcomers.)    So, if you want to grab a decent burger and fries while in , give this place a try.   Review #159

This International House of Pancakes on Mt. Holly Road, , , sits in a renovated former fast food structure, and is small compared to the more recent versions of this franchise around the country. All the cues are there to prepare you for a hearty breakfast.   I walked in before court  for a light bite and coffee, and to kill some time before my workday began. I took a seat at the 5 stool counter and was served by , a young dude who seemed diligent and engaging. After a short look at the long menu, I opted for their traditional  toast and strong java. All the other choices seemed like they would be way too sweet with berries and whipped cream. Didn't want those calories.   My plate arrived  looking attractive and tempting. I spread the cup of butter across the egg pocked surface, and poured on the old fashioned syrup (maple not on the counter).  First bite was very good, but a realized that their signature approach to this dish was to add pancake mix to the beaten eggs.  This was visible in the unusual shine on the surface of the toast, as well as the distinct mild taste of buttermilk with each forkful. I had not tasted this before, but I enjoyed this take on a historic platter.  Nice for a change of pace, but not something I would specifically request, as I prefer the traditional approach to  toast.   The carafe of hot coffee in front of me is another thing they do well. They realize that coffee is an inexpensive way to appear generous.   I have never been a IHOP regular, as I normally prefer a mom and pop shop to a chain or franchise for breakfast, or any meal. Still, I appreciate what they do, and their effort to find a new approach to their business. They even are doing burgers now. Haven't tried them, but they do look good on the menu.

I decided to go with a flight (4 five ounce selections) which have varying prices dependent upon the brews selected (anywhere between $8-14 for the four choices). The PB&C, a peanut butter imperial stout was full of peanut flavor and was quite good as a special choice.  The Color Blind (blonde stout 7.8%) was another smooth and full flavored choice.  I also enjoyed the Kuppa Kopi (coffee porter 5.7%) for its smooth coffee taste without the bitterness.  I would drink each of these again!  My only choice that didn't taste quite so appealing was the Victimless Crime, an oatmeal stout orange zest.  Something about it seemed like an odd pairing the more I drank.  Even though it was only 5.3%, it seemed more boozy than the others to me, and the orange flavor when paired with the other flavors in the profile, just didn't appeal to me.  Still, 3 out of 4 ain't bad.    It can be a little tricky getting in and out of the parking lot since it is located at such a busy intersection (96th and ).  I managed to time traffic okay to head west on 96th to leave, but trying to get back on the interstate or to head east on 96th during rush hour would seem difficult due to excess traffic.  Enjoy the beer, but keep your wits about you when you head out!  Review #426

There is a large parking lot on the south end of the park.  As with any low lying property at creekside, I can imagine you need to watch the weather if you are planning on hiking around here after heavy rains (the last major flooding was in ).  The trails are paved for conservation purposes, hoping that hikers will stay on them.  The park is not part of the city's park system, but ran independently by the Lion's Club.  Still, it is a welcome addition to the areas green spaces.  Review #710

If  Archie & Veronica malt shops and Back to the Future big fin  road steel move your imagination, then Jem's Restaurant in , , may be for you.   What from the outside looks like another shopping center fast food luncheonette constrained by its surroundings to be a boring food dealer, is in fact a real trip down memory lane. The joint is a museum of cultural artifacts from  of television, with large posters of Rebel Without a Cause, , and Seven Year Itch, . Perhaps that's why the room was full with retirees and people over  (except for those of us needing to eat and run). This place is the original greasy spoon, for all the right reasons.   The double "U" counter separated the kitchen from the dining room. My spinner faced the grill operated by two short order cooks who worked smoothly in tandem. I ordered coffee and Jem's Scramble with feta and rye toast. The full insulated carafe of java set in front of me was a nice touch. I listened to the repartee between customers and servers. It was familiar and entertaining. Most everyone seemed to be a regular.   I noted the pile of chunk cut red bliss potatoes and metal tray of bacon on the grill. I watched eggs, pancakes,  toast and breakfast sandwiches being cooked and constructed as spatulas flew. I also saw that the grill was not scaped clean between orders, allowing residue from everything grilled there to build up and become part of the next dish. No judgement. Then, my small Scramble arrived, steaming in my face and fogging my glasses. Smelled awesome and looked like a gently beckoning glistening syren.   It was delicious. The eggs held the sausage, onions, peppers and feta in a wet/warm embrace, allowing each forkful to hang together with all elements dancing on my tongue. There was also a hint of everything else that came before, making for a mysterious, yet very pleasant flavor.   Maybe that is the house secret to success, or just how it accidentally became an amazing greasy spoon. Intentional or not, Jem's has a full house , and is definitely doing something right.

They used to not have a corkage fee but the last time I ate there it was around $8 per bottle.  I can go to lots of other better places that serve much bigger portions of food at lower prices that don't charge any corkage fee.  I don't mind paying a corkage fee in a nice restaurant that already sells wine but this place is a far cry from fine dining and has no alcohol permit.  I love  tapas but I just seem to strongly dislike   tapas as it seems I find most of it BLAH.  If you like this type of food you should be quite happy here but it just isn't my style of food... I think it might be because they don't use aioli and lack the power of enough GARLIC in their food!

This is a cute place and much-needed for the area it is in.  The beer selection is decent but the food... needs work.  The menu is very small and the way things are presented make it seem like they are trying too hard to be upscale.  The nachos in particular were a huge disappointment.  I didn't know it was possible to screw up a standard plate of bar nachos until  at Devil's Den.  After seeing a couple plates go by, we decided to order them.  We hadn't noticed an abundance of salsa, so we specifically asked for some on the side.  This is how the conversation went:  me: we'll have the nachos with a side of salsa server: (weird look)...okay...   later  server: we don't have salsa... is fresh pico okay? me: that would be great!   later  server: um, we can't do pico either.  How about a free side of guacamole? me: um, okay  Who serves nachos without salsa or anything resembling salsa?    Devil's Den does.    For the record, ketchup is not really good on nachos...

There is a good reason that Iaria's has been in business for a long time: they serve a good meal!  I stopped in for lunch after parking in their private lot on the north side of the building.  (The doors are somewhat tough to open due to vacuum pressure, so pull hard!)  At the doorway, there is a hostess station sign asking you to wait to be seated.  To the right is a hallway that leads to the bar area.  I opted for the dining room since the bar looked somewhat cramped and packed.  The dining room has a wall of mirrors on the far end to make the space seem more open.  There are 4-top tables with chairs and some booth style seats.  The booths look padded, but be careful to not sit too hard.  The "padding" doesn't do much to protect you from the hard, uneven seating underneath.  (I tried scooting in to a corner and caught a raised joint where the benches were together.)  The waitress was pleasant and though handling a large group at the tables next to me, minimized the wait between interactions.  My water was refilled and my check was processed in a timely manner.  I went with one of the lunch specials, the beef lasagna.  It came with a side salad as part of the deal.  First, I received a complementary basket of sliced bread and crackers.  The bread came with room temperature margarine and there was already a bottle of olive oil on the table.  The salad was next and the  dressing I ordered was in a cup on the side with a spoon to allow me to put as much as I wanted over the salad. The dressing was really good and may have been made in house.   The salad plate was 8" and was made using iceberg lettuce that was mostly cold and crisp.  However, some of the ingredients didn't look quite in top shape due to possibly too cold temperatures.   The lasagna was served unadorned in a bowl that allowed extra sauce to be held in reserve for when needed.  The noodles were very tender and the beef was lightly seasoned.  The flavor was good but not layered like I've had other places.  The sauce worked quite well with the beef and noodles.  The portion was appropriate for a lunch portion too.  I was satisfied without feeling stuffed.  Overall, I enjoyed my return visit to Iaria's.  Lunch was quick, service friendly, and reasonably priced for the meal.  Review #1033

I don't know.  Maybe I'm a snob when it comes to oysters and seafood in general, but I was left underwhelmed by my experience here.  My friends ordered a dozen oysters; half raw and half char broiled.  I ordered the seafood etouffee.  I tried the oysters, but I immediately noticed that they weren't very big.  The char broiled oysters were good and had a nice buttery flavor.  My etouffee was ok, but not really anything special.  The prices here seem a little bit steep for what seems to be just a casual dining place.  I will say that one of my friends ordered the seafood platter, which came with fried crab, catfish, oysters and fries.  It was huge, looked really good, and can definitely be split between two people.  The service was good and we were seated quickly, with only about a ten minute wait.  Given the choice, I would probably go somewhere else for my oyster needs.  I'd be more inclined to support a small local business, rather than this chain.

Anyway, I went to my regular PJ's  and they not only honored the coupon, but they told me that it can be honored at any PJ's and the folks at this place screwed up.
